items.t: TDEE calculator in kg or lb
items.d: Pick metric (kg, cm) or imperial (lb, ft, in). Imperial values are converted with 1 lb = 0.4536 kg and 1 in = 2.54 cm before the equation, so the result is the same either way: a 35-year-old woman of 165 cm and 60 kg, or 5 ft 5 in and 132 lb, gets a BMR of 1,295 kcal and a sedentary TDEE of 1,554 kcal.

The Mifflin-St Jeor equation adds 5 kcal for men and subtracts 161 kcal for women, so at the same age, height and weight a woman's BMR is 166 kcal lower. After the activity factor, the gap is about 199 kcal (sedentary) to 315 kcal (extra active).
At 180 cm and 80 kg, BMR is 1,780 kcal and TDEE is 2,136 kcal sedentary, 2,759 kcal moderately active and 3,382 kcal extra active.
Each year of age lowers BMR by 5 kcal before the activity factor: about 50 kcal of BMR per decade, or 60 to 95 kcal of TDEE depending on the activity level.
